props.title: The Witches

sections.content: The Witches (1990) stands as one of the most terrifying children's films ever made, masterfully bringing Roald Dahl's dark fantasy to life through Jim Henson's practical effects and Anjelica Huston's commanding performance. The film follows Dahl's signature blend of whimsy and horror, much like Matilda (1996) and James and the Giant Peach (1996), but director Nicolas Roeg pushes the frightening elements further than most family films dare. The practical transformation sequences, where witches reveal their true grotesque forms, remain unsettling even by today's CGI standards.

sections.content: The film's treatment of childhood fears resonates with other dark children's classics like The Dark Crystal (1982) and Return to Oz (1985). What sets The Witches apart is its refusal to sugar-coat its ending - the protagonist remains a mouse, breaking from Hollywood's typical insistence on complete resolution. This faithfulness to Dahl's original vision creates a more impactful story about accepting change and finding happiness despite permanent transformation.

Anjelica Huston's Grand High Witch ranks among cinema's greatest villains, combining glamorous sophistication with genuine menace. Her performance influenced later family-film antagonists like Glenn Close in 101 Dalmatians (1996) and Cate Blanchett in Cinderella (2015). The practical makeup effects by Jim Henson's Creature Shop represent a high point in pre-digital creature design, alongside their work in Labyrinth (1986). SUBHEAD: Impact on Dark Children's Cinema

sections.content: The Witches helped pave the way for more sophisticated children's horror, influencing films like ParaNorman (2012) and Monster House (2006). Its balance of humor and genuine scares demonstrated that family films didn't need to shy away from darker themes. The practical effects work, particularly during the witch convention scene, set a standard that even modern films struggle to match, proving that tangible puppetry and makeup can create more visceral reactions than CGI.
